Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:12: The fourth blemish is "and turn away from you." This matter may be explained as it is explained at the end of the portion of Noach (76a) regarding the Shechinah: when a person is blemished, the Shechinah withdraws from him. So too it is explained in the Tikkunim (52b) - their words: "and if the soul is sullied by sins, or diminishes from itself even one of the commandments - as the masters of the Mishnah established, 'a transgression extinguishes a mitzvah' - in that place where the transgression dwells and the mitzvah is removed from it, that limb is blemished, and it is a defect of the soul; because of it the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon the soul, as it is said (Leviticus 21:18) 'any man who has a defect shall not draw near' - a soul that has a defect in its two hundred and forty-eight commandments is not drawn near to Him because of it" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:13: Along these lines it may be explained here: "for the Lord your God walks," etc. It is the way of the Shechinah to walk before a person to guard him, as is explained in the portion of Shelach Lecha (166a), and it is the way of a person to walk behind the Shechinah, as it says (Deuteronomy 13:5) "you shall walk after the Lord your God." When a person causes a blemish, she withdraws from before him and turns to his rear, and thus he has no protection before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:14: However, what appears from the language brought afterward, "and therefore, 'you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife' - why? because it is written 'it is your father's nakedness,'" and it explains that the blemish reaches Tiferet as well - if so, it appears that this too is mentioned in the verse, just as "unseemly thing" was mentioned; namely, "the nakedness of your father's wife" also corresponds to "it is your father's nakedness," mentioned in "and turn away from you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:15: The matter is that when the Shechinah is blemished on account of man's sin, Tiferet withdraws from her, because she is a throne for Him, and He does not rest upon a throne that is incomplete; and so it is explained in the portion of Vayikra (4b), and likewise in the Tikkunim, concerning "and he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside" [Joseph and Potiphar's wife].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:16: Along these lines, it is explained in the Tikkunim (146b) - their words: "In this way the Holy One, blessed be He, drives away the Shechinah and casts her from His house - this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 50:1) 'and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.' Now, is it not so that whoever honors her in exile honors the Holy One, blessed be He, and whoever demeans her demeans the Holy One, blessed be He? Therefore (I Samuel 2:30) 'for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt'" - so far. The reason for this is that they are both two faces of one countenance, and a king without a queen is not a king, as Rashbi explains (Vayikra 5a) on "Great is the Lord and greatly praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain" (Psalms 48:2): "it is heard that a king without a queen is not a king, is not great, and is not praised" - so far. And likewise it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim 117b), that the demeaning of the Matronita [Queen] is when people demean her place, and this is her disgrace - so far. And this statement, "the demeaning of the Matronita is when they demean her place," will be explained, with the Lord's help, in the matter of the blemish to the Throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:17: What is meant by "and turn away from you" is explained by Rashbi (Shelach 165a): "Ah, the holy pious one, whoever keeps the covenant places it behind him and stands before it; and if you say, whoever keeps [the covenant] is behind [it] - behold, the guarding is greater and more supernal than everything that guards it - and who is this? The supernal righteous one [Yesod], who with great love enters between Tzedek [Malchut, feminine 'righteousness'] and Tzaddik [masculine 'righteous'], and is thus found guarded from every side; happy is one who keeps this covenant" - so far. And further on there (166a) it is proven that when a person is righteous, he walks behind the Shechinah, because the Shechinah walks before him to guard him, as it is written (Exodus 23:20) "behold, I send an angel before you to guard you," and the person stands at the level of the righteous one, and thus he is behind her - this is [the meaning of] "you shall walk after the Lord your God." And their statement (see Zohar there; Berachot 61a) "a man should not walk behind a woman" means that he should not descend below into the world of the feminine, along the lines of Abraham, of whom it is said (Genesis 17:1) "walk before Me," and it is explained there that this is because he had neither circumcision nor peri'ah [uncovering], and it is a diminishment - "he turned back [shav] from following Me" (I Samuel 15:11), meaning he descended from the level of the masculine; this is what is said there, "there was no 'behind,' because he was not uncovered," see there. With this we understand "and turn away from you": for the masculine one, who walks behind you to guard you, withdraws from you because you caused a blemish to his feminine counterpart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:18: We may also say that "behind you" [achareicha] refers to the Shechinah, who is called "back" [achor], as it says (Exodus 33:23) "and you shall see My back"; and Tiferet turns away from her on account of the blemish. The first interpretation seems to me the primary one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:19: Nevertheless, it is possible to combine both interpretations as one, and say that certainly it is never possible for the [divine] unity to be entirely severed, for although it says (Deuteronomy 23:15) "the Lord your God" refers to the Shechinah (in the Zohar cited above, 75a), Tiferet is also present there, as it says "the Lord, He is God" (Deuteronomy 4:35); and therefore it says "for the Lord your God walks," etc. - both together, in unity, walking, etc.; and therefore it says "to save you and to deliver your enemies," etc. - a double protection for both of them. And it was explained above that she [the Shechinah] is called "the guarding of the way," and Tiferet comes to guard her, as it says (Isaiah 42:8) "I am the Lord, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another." Since He comes to guard her, His face is turned toward her back, in the manner of a guard who protects from behind, and Israel is in between, as it says, "whoever keeps the covenant enters between Tzaddik and Tzedek." And when it says "His face is turned toward her back," the meaning is the face of mercy and good providence to bestow upon her, for "back" indicates withdrawal and concealment - the proof being Adam and Eve, that when they were back to back there was no union. Here, in the matter of guarding, there is no union, but rather a manner of bestowal; therefore He commanded that one not blemish the Shechinah, since this would cause the withdrawal of Tiferet from her, and turn His face away from her such that they would be back to back - this is "and turn away from you" without qualification, applying both to the Shechinah, who is called "back," and to the person who is in between, whose back is toward the masculine one. Thus four aspects concerning the blemish have been explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:20: We saw fit to complete the explanation of the passage, since it pertains to our discourse concerning the blemish of the Shechinah: it says that for three things Israel is delayed in exile - using the word "delayed," since the exile of the Shechinah was decreed for only a thousand years, as it is said (Lamentations 1:13) "He has made me desolate, faint all the day," as is also explained in the portion of Vaera (Shemot 17a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:21: The first: "because they treat the Shechinah with contempt in exile" - meaning, because they profane the Name of the Lord, as it is said (Ezekiel 36:20) "when it was said of them, 'these are the people of the Lord, and yet they have gone out of His land'"; and when Israel does something that involves a profanation of the Divine Name, there is no greater disgrace to the Shechinah than this - it is like a parable of a father with a son, and the son does improper things to people, so that people say, "cursed is the one who bore this child, cursed is the one who raised him." This applies to the whole nation in general, and in particular to every individual in Israel who transgresses what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him - he causes disgrace above, to the Shechinah, since Scripture says (Isaiah 50:1) "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away." And as a person adds transgression, he adds exile and banishment, for above they say, "see the mother, what children she has raised! It would be fitting, God forbid, that she be banished outside the palace, since she did not discipline her son to be proper" - and similarly, our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yalkut Bereishit, remez 8, and see remez 27) concerning the nine curses with which the earth was cursed (Tikkunei Zohar 95b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:22: Further, it may be as is explained (Tikkunei Zohar 146b) in "honor your father and your mother": "your father" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He; "your mother" - this is the Shechinah; fear of her is through the negative commandments, honor of her through the positive commandments, of which it is said "for those who honor Me I will honor," and likewise all who transgress the negative commandments, of them it is said "and those who demean Me shall be treated with contempt" - so far, as relevant to us. We find, then, that the contempt of the Shechinah is that they do not accord her the honor due to her through the positive commandments, and transgress the negative commandments. Now, in all the ways that a person is obligated to honor his earthly father and mother, so too, similarly, he is obligated to honor his supernal Father and Mother; and just as one is warned against demeaning the honor of one's earthly father and mother, upon which stands the curse - as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:16) "cursed be he who dishonors his father and his mother" - and the Rambam writes (Laws of Rebels, chapter 5) that even by a mere gesture - so too one must be careful not to demean the honor of one's supernal Father and Mother, and to be careful of everything pertaining to their honor. Of this kind, it appears that one must be careful of what Rashbi says (Terumah 131b; see Hashmatot 256a), that one who speaks in the synagogue causes disrespect to the supernal arrangement above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:23: The second: "and turn their faces away from the Shechinah" - this has both a general and a particular sense. The general sense is that the wicked turn back and turn their faces away from the Shechinah, saying with their mouths that they do not wish to have a share in the God of Israel. The particular sense is one who interrupts words of Torah for idle matters, since one who occupies himself with Torah has his face turned toward the Shechinah, as our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 18; see Tamid 32b) on the verse (Lamentations 2:19) "pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord" - and he interrupts, thus turning his face away from the Shechinah. Similarly, one who is praying and interrupts in the middle - even if it is [merely] during the Zemirot [songs of praise] - especially if it is during the silent Amidah, and in the middle of his prayer turns his face to look here and there for his own needs - certainly this touches upon the honor of the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:24: The third: "and because they defile themselves before the Shechinah" - one must be careful of this in everything the Torah explicitly mentions as impurity, such as the impurity of forbidden foods, as it is said (Leviticus 11:43) "do not make your souls detestable through any creeping thing that creeps, and do not defile yourselves with them, lest you become defiled through them"; impurity through forbidden sexual relations (ibid. 18:24) "do not defile yourselves with any of these, for the nations were defiled by all of these," etc.; and one must be careful of the impurity of the menstruant woman.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:25: Impurity through skin afflictions [nega'im], and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that such afflictions come as a punishment for slander (Arachin 16a). And Rashbi explains (Metzora 53a): "Rabbi Chiya said, whoever speaks slander, all his limbs become defiled," etc. And in the portion of Shemini (41a): "a person should not blemish his mouth and his tongue, and how much more so should he not defile his soul and himself, for he becomes defiled in the other world" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:26: Also the impurity of idolatry, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26) "you shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it." What is relevant here is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Tetzaveh 182a), which we shall quote below, that one who becomes angry defiles himself inside and out, like idolatry itself, and of one who is angry it is said (Exodus 34:17) "you shall not make for yourself molten gods" - meaning that he literally makes himself into an idol. So too the one who is haughty is likewise, and so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Mechilta, portion of Yitro) on the verse (Exodus 20:18) "and Moses drew near to the thick darkness" - their words: "anyone who is haughty of heart causes the land to become defiled and the Shechinah to depart, as it is said (Psalms 101:5) 'him who has a haughty eye and a proud heart I cannot endure'; all who are haughty of heart are called an abomination, as it is said (Proverbs 16:5) 'every haughty heart is an abomination to the Lord.' Idolatry is called an abomination, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26) 'and you shall not bring an abomination into your house' - just as idolatry defiles the land and causes the Shechinah to depart," etc. - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:27: Also one must be careful of the impurity of emitting seed in vain, for this sin blemishes the Shechinah, and therefore it says "before the Shechinah." Rashbi explains (Vayeshev 188a) that there is no sin that defiles a person more than one who emits seed in vain - his words: "Come and see: among all the sins by which a person defiles himself in this world, this is the sin by which a person is defiled the most, in this world and in the world to come - whoever spills his seed vainly and brings forth seed in vain, by hand or by foot, and defiles himself thereby - as it is said (Psalms 5:5) 'for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.' For this reason he does not enter behind the curtain and does not see the countenance of the Ancient of Days, as we learn: it is written here 'evil shall not dwell with you,' and it is written (Genesis 38:7) 'and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the Lord' [understood as referring to this sin]. And therefore it is written (Isaiah 1:15) 'your hands are full of blood.' Happy is the portion of the person who fears his Master and guards himself from the evil way, and purifies himself, to engage in the fear of his Master" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:28: There is also another impurity, although impurity is not mentioned explicitly in the Torah in this regard: one who has relations with his wife not in the natural manner. This is treated stringently in the Zohar, portion of Pekudei (259a) - their words: "Concerning this we learn: whoever has relations with his bed from behind [i.e., unnaturally] weakens the arrangement of face-to-face gazing that illuminates everything together, and [prevents] everything from being found face to face in proper union, as it is said (Genesis 2:24) 'and he shall cleave to his wife' - to his wife specifically, and not to his wife's back" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:29: In these three matters the word "Shechinah" is mentioned in each one, because she is called "Shechinah" [Indwelling Presence] on account of her dwelling among the lower beings, and specifically among Israel, as it is said (Exodus 34:9) "let my Lord, I pray, go in our midst," and as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (see Berachot 7a): he [Moses] asked that the Shechinah rest upon Israel and not upon the idolatrous nations, and the Holy One, blessed be He, agreed to it. And whoever transgresses one of these matters, the Shechinah stands against him and he has no shame of countenance, and he causes the exile to be prolonged - for Israel was not exiled until they said, "we have no portion in David... every man to his tents [le-ohalecha], O Israel" (II Chronicles 10:16) - do not read "le-ohalecha" [to his tents] but "le-elohecha" [to his gods] (see Yalkut Shmuel, remez 106; Tanchuma, Beshalach 16) - and they denied the God of Israel; and one who sins in the matters mentioned is like one who denies [divine] providence, and rather than being disciplined in exile for what he was the cause of, it is fitting, God forbid, that he be further delayed in exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:30: Let us return to the discourse with which we began this chapter, that one must fear not to blemish the Shechinah, which is the "unseemly thing" we explained; there are yet two further aspects concerning the blemish to her, explained in the Tikkunim and in Ra'aya Meheimna.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:31: In the Tikkunim (49b) it says that the "heart" is the Shechinah, and there are in the heart two chambers, one the dwelling place of the good inclination and the other the dwelling place of the evil inclination; and it says that the good inclination is the Shechinah in the aspects we shall explain - its words: "'Heart understands, heart knows, heart sees' - she is the Shechinah, who takes only the pure part, which is the offering of pure prayer, without bran and without refuse, and offers it to her husband, the beauty of all; but the liver's lobe she does not give to her husband, only remnants and refuse - and who is her husband [in this negative image]? The spleen, 'another god.' And from these remnants that she takes, the blood of the spleen is made, dark and black, and this is the deceitful serpent that seduced Eve, who is the heart, and caused her death. Now, there are two chambers of the heart - which of them does it seduce? Rather, that of the left, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:2) 'a fool's heart is to his left' - and of it is said (ibid. 7:26) 'and I find more bitter than death the woman.' 'A wise man's heart is to his right' - this is 'a woman of valor, the crown of her husband,' of whom it is said (Proverbs 18:22) 'he who finds a wife finds good' - for she is the good inclination, a person's good fortune, of whom it is said (Ezekiel 44:30) 'to cause a blessing to rest on your house' - 'the blessing of the Lord, it enriches' (Proverbs 10:22) - and of her it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:9) 'see life with the wife whom you love'" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:32: The intent that emerges from the whole of his words, without dwelling on every phrase, is that "heart" unqualified refers to the Shechinah, and there are in her two chambers: one, on the side of the right, is the dwelling place of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at; the other, on the side of the left, draws from the judgment of Gevurah, and it is from the side of the left that the fool is grasped for his portion below, since all the external forces [kelipot] are found below on the left side, in the unfolding of the levels. This is [the meaning of] "a wise man's heart is to his right and a fool's heart is to his left" - for whoever wishes to become wise should turn to the right, and thus wisdom comes to him precisely through his right side. His being the dwelling place of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at is alluded to by his bringing three verses: the first, corresponding to Da'at, which is in the middle, "a woman of valor, the crown of her husband" - this is a person's good fortune [mazal], and so it is explained in the Tikkunim (99b) - their words: "the supernal Vav, which is the supernal mazal that ascends in thought." And corresponding to Binah, of her it is said "to cause a blessing to rest on your house; the blessing of the Lord, it enriches," and it is explained in the Tikkunim (27a) that this is Binah. And corresponding to Chochmah, which is life, it says "see life with the wife whom you love," for love is on the right. And although above I explained in the name of Rashbi that the good inclination unqualified is on the right, the intent is the right arm, which comprises three joints, namely Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at, as is explained in the Idra (Naso 142a-b), "let the unspecified be learned from the specified."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:33: With this we understand a second interpretation of the passage we quoted from the portion of Bereishit concerning fear, "why is it called 'the fear of the Lord'? because it is the tree of good and evil," etc. This is explained: it is the secret of the heart, the dwelling place of good, which is the right, while evil is the secret of judgment, and the evil itself flows downward through the unfolding of the levels. "If a person merits" he cleaves to her in the aspect of her right side, which is the good inclination in the aspects mentioned; "if he did not merit," behold, evil cleaves to him in the secret of "a fool's heart is to his left."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:34: One must fear the enticements of his inclination, lest he cleave to the spleen, "another god," which is the serpent that draws near to the heart and causes it death. Along these lines, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Tzav 28b), in a passage we shall quote below, that says: "the sin-offering [chatat] is the liver's lobe, which weighs upon it with the sins, the sullying, of Israel's transgressions, in the manner that the liver makes heavy the blood, the dregs, upon the arteries of the heart" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:35: It is explained in the Tikkunim (133a) that whoever is ruled by his inclination is completely wicked - their words: "My son, all this is the secret of the transmigration of the evil inclination: there is one for whom it resembles a lion, and one for whom it resembles a serpent, and one for whom it resembles a donkey - it changes for all creatures according to their deeds and according to the hour in which they were made. Nevertheless, happy is the soul that rules over it and rides upon it, like a man who rides upon his horse or his donkey; woe to him over whom, if it is like a serpent, it rules - this one is called completely wicked; and whoever rules over it is completely righteous, of whom it is said (Isaiah 43:4) 'and I will give men in your place, and peoples for your life' - for when a person rules over his inclination, he thereby rules over all who hate him, but if his inclination rules over him, those who hate him rule over him" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:36: It says at the end of the passage that when a person rules over his inclination, he likewise rules over his enemies - this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said on (Proverbs 16:7) "when the ways of a man please the Lord, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him," quoted in Bereishit Rabbah, cited in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 954), on this verse: Rabbi Yochanan said, "his enemies" refers to his wife; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, this refers to the evil inclination, etc.; Rabbi Berachyah said, "even his enemies" includes the pests of his house, such as fleas, gnats, and flies.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:37: The reason for all this is that when a person strengthens the good inclination over the evil inclination, so too is judgment subdued beneath mercy; and when the supernal root of judgment is sweetened, all the lower branches that flow from the root of Gevurah are all turned to mercy - this is [the meaning of] "when the ways of a man please the Lord" - that the secret of Ratzon [will/favor] is bestowed upon "the ways of a man," which is Ze'ir Anpin - "the Lord is a man of war" (Exodus 15:3; Zohar I 60a) - and there is the source of judgment (see Zohar III 142b) - "even his enemies He makes to be at peace with him," as I have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:38: It is impossible for a person to attain this level unless he repents fully and subdues his inclination to the utmost degree of subjugation, and subdues the attribute of judgment within him, as I explained in the previous chapter; and by this he causes the drawing down of the flow of Ratzon to subdue all the masters of judgment who accuse him, as is explained in the Idra of Naso (129a), that with the revelation of the "forehead of favor," all wraths are stilled - these being called "enemies" above; when a person subdues judgment, he causes the drawing down of the flow of Ratzon to still the lower judgments of this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:39: Further, concerning the matter of the blemish a person causes to the Shechinah, it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Tzav 28a-b): it says there that the wings of the dove are the positive commandments, through which she flies upward, and it says afterward: these negative commandments are her constraints, like birds caught in a snare, and all her constraints that prevent her from flying are called "adhesions" [sirchot], like adhesions that prevent the lung's wings from being blown [i.e., inflated]. So too, the guilt [asham] of Israel takes hold of the wings of the Shechinah, which are the Chayot of the Throne, so that it should not ascend through the merits of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He, and their sins weigh down and burden her wings, and the guilt is the "Mother" of the mixed multitude - an adhesion that takes hold of the Throne, where the Matronita is, and does not allow her to ascend from exile, and merits take hold of her to raise her, and she remains hanging in the air, like an adhesion hanging in the air - and this is the central pillar, which is the air; so too the ["suspended"] guilt-offering hangs upon the righteous one [Yesod], who is bound between heaven and earth. The sin-offering is the liver's lobe, which weighs upon it with the sins, the sullying, of Israel's transgressions, in the manner that the liver makes heavy the blood, the dregs, upon the arteries of the heart. So too these sins weigh upon the wings of the Shechinah, which are the positive commandments, resembling the wings of a dove; but the negative commandments, when they weigh upon the positive ones - that is, when Israel's transgressions are more numerous than their merits - it is said in the Torah, which is the body, (Daniel 8:12) "and it cast down truth to the ground," and she cries out, "the Lord has given me into hands from which I cannot rise" (Lamentations 1:14), "she has fallen, she shall no longer rise" (Amos 5:2). Therefore the Tannaim and Amoraim instituted prayers in place of sacrifices, to remove sin-offerings and guilt-offerings from her" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:40: It is explained in the passage that there are two aspects to the blemish: the first is the blemish of the Shechinah, which is what is said at the end of the passage, "these sins weigh upon the wings of the Shechinah, which are the positive commandments." There is also a blemish reaching Tiferet, "and it cast down truth to the ground," as will be explained further concerning the blemish that reaches Him. And the Shechinah cries out, "the Lord has given me into hands from which I cannot rise." Therefore one must fear his own deeds, and not cause, through his deeds, the outcry of the Shechinah against him and her falling to the ground, as it is written (Amos 5:2) "she has fallen, she shall no longer rise."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:41: Further, in this passage is explained the matter of the blemish to the Throne, as it says that the adhesions grasp the Chayot of the Throne and the Throne itself, and the Shechinah is clothed in the Throne, and when there is an adhesion there, she does not ascend above through the merits of Israel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:42: Here, in this chapter, is explained the root of fear, an additional elaboration on what was said in the portion of Bereishit, "why is it called the fear of the Lord? because it is the tree of good and evil." Everything beneath it is called the tree of knowledge of good and evil, since it says in Ra'aya Meheimna (above, portion of Tzav, 28b) that the adhesion grasps the Throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:43: Close to this aspect of fear from the portion of Bereishit is what is explained in the Tikkunim (77a) - their words: "there is fear and there is fear: 'the fear of the Lord' - this is the Shechinah, the holy kingship [Malchut]; 'evil fear' - this is the strap for lashing the wicked, and what is it? The deadly poison of Samael, his female counterpart. 'The fear of the Lord' is a reward for whoever keeps the negative commandments; 'evil fear' is the strap for lashing whoever transgresses them" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:44: Our intent in this is explained by his saying, "'the fear of the Lord' is a reward for whoever keeps the negative commandments" - this is the essence of fear: that one not transgress a negative commandment and thereby give the outer forces room to blemish and breach the fence to enter within - besides the several aspects already explained and yet to be explained, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:1: Since our explanation in the previous chapter of the root of fear preceded, and we said that it means a person distancing himself from the evil inclination to draw near to the good, we saw fit to append this chapter to explain that one should not merely disregard the enticements of his inclination but should overcome it, so that he be called a mighty one who conquers his inclination - this being one of the aspects of fear, for we find fear in Gevurah as well as in Binah. Fear in Gevurah is explained in the Tikkunim (10b), that Malchut is called "the fear of the Lord" from the side of Gevurah, and "love" from the side of Chesed; and in Tikkun 2/3 (18b) it explains fear in Binah explicitly, saying that this is the meaning of (Avot 3:17) "if there is no fear, there is no wisdom."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:2: The matter, as I explained in the previous chapter, is that one must always fear not to arouse the inclination and judgment, and the [evil] inclination flows from the supernal root of judgment of these two attributes [Gevurah and Binah], as Rashbi explains (Noach 70b) on the verse (Genesis 8:21) "I will not again [curse the ground]" - that from these two attributes the root of judgment comes. And a person's overcoming his inclination flows to him from Gevurah, as is likewise explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 10a): "in the fifth month, strength is given in Gevurah to overcome the evil inclination, from the side of Samael, so that it does not rule over him," etc. - and there the discussion concerns the nine months of gestation of the soul of our righteous Messiah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:3: Further, in the Tikkunim (1b), explaining the matter of six levels, that there are pious ones, mighty ones, masters of Torah, etc., it says: "mighty ones" - from the side of Gevurah, who give strength to their masters to subdue the servant beneath his master and the maidservant beneath her mistress, through the binding of the tefillin - so far. We find, then, that from the side of Gevurah, those who conquer their inclination are called "mighty ones," and this is the reality of fear - to always fear lest the servant become unrestrained and breach the fence, but rather remain bound and subdued beneath his master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:4: This matter is further explained in the Zohar (Vayeshev 189b), on the verse (Psalms 103:20) "Bless the Lord, His angels, mighty in strength," etc., and how much a person must overcome his inclination every single day - their words: "Rabbi Chiya opened and said, 'Bless the Lord, His angels, mighty in strength,' etc. Come and see how much a person must guard himself from his sins and walk in a proper way, so that the evil inclination not lead him astray, since it accuses him every single day, as we have said; and since it accuses him constantly, a person must fortify himself against it and rise up in a place of strength, for he must be victorious over it and join with the place of Gevurah - for when a person fortifies himself against it, he is then on the side of Gevurah and cleaves to it to fortify himself. And since that evil inclination is mighty, a person must be mightier than it; and those who fortify themselves against it are called 'mighty in strength,' each kind matching its counterpart - and these are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, who come from the strict side of Gevurah to fortify themselves against it, 'mighty in strength, who do His word'" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:5: What he says, "then he is on the side of Gevurah and cleaves to it to fortify himself," is to indicate what is being expounded, that being called a "mighty one who conquers his inclination" is from the side of Gevurah. And Scripture adds "mighty in strength," for one's strength must be greater than the strength of the evil inclination, and this is what it says, "a person must be mightier than it"; and without doubt, that Gevurah overcomes the evil inclination is from the power of Binah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (85b), that strength [koach] is in Binah, although this is not stated explicitly in this passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:6: It says, "and these are the angels of the Holy One, blessed be He, who come," etc., because the angels were created on the second day (Sefer HaBahir, letter 21), and it is explained in Sefer HaBahir that all the angels were created from the fire of Gevurah (see letter 145); we find, then, that the righteous one who conquers his inclination is equal to an angel in this respect.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:7: Although our Sages, of blessed memory, said, in Tractate Sukkah, chapter HaChalil (52b): Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, a person's inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it is said (Psalms 37:32) "the wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him," and were it not for the Holy One, blessed be He, helping him, he could not overcome it, as it is said, "the Lord will not abandon him into his hand," etc. - it appears that a person's help in overcoming his inclination comes from the Holy One, blessed be He, and what praise is there for the righteous? But the matter is that in all things, an arousal from below must always come first, as they said in the Zohar several times (Emor 108(110)b): "arousal below produces arousal above." This is the praise of the righteous one: that he is the one who begins, and afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him - and this is the very nature of the word "help" [ezer], like a person who is occupied with a burden and cannot manage it, and his fellow comes and helps him.
